 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error lies in the part 'attend'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Hardly had he come out of the (1)/ cinema hall then the bomb exploded (2)/ and shattered the hall completely. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Hardly' and 'when' are **correlative conjunctions**.
 
• **Correlative conjunctions** are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in **pairs**, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another.
 
 
• For example: **Hardly** had I reached the station **when **the train left.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, as 'Hardly' is present in part (1) of the sentence, the correlative conjunction that must be used in (2) should be 'when'.
 
• Hence, 'then' should be replaced by 'when' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Hardly had he come out of the cinema hall** when** the bomb exploded and shattered the hall completely.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Some of the important Correlative Conjunctions are:
 
 
• Either….or
 
• Neither….nor
 
• **Hardly….when**
 
• Scarcely….when
 
• Both…and
 
• If…then
 
• Not only….but also
 
• Rather….than
 
• Whether…or
 
• No sooner…than
 
• Else…but
 
• Lest…should
 
• Other…than
 
• So…that

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Because copper prices are going down (1)/ demand for alternative (2)/ products to copper are lessening. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct **answer is '3'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

**Let's look at the following points-**

 
• The **subject** must agree in number with its **verb**.
 
• If the **subject** is **singular**, then its **verb** must also be **singular** and **vice**-**versa**.
 
 
• **For e.g.-***** **The wildlife of Africa **attract **many tourists annually. **(X) ***
 
 

* The wildlife of Africa** attracts** many tourists annually. ***(✓)**

 
• *In the given sentence, the verb should be used according to the subject of the sentence, as the subject is singular i.e. demand, it will follow the singular form of verb i.e. 'is'.*

 

**The correct sentence- ***Because copper prices are going down demand for alternative products to copper** is** lessening.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Welter
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **turmoil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word similar in meaning to **Welter **is "Turmoil".
 
• Let's have a look at the meaning of the words given in the question:-
 
• **Welter **means** a state of confusion, chaos or turmoil.**
 
 
• Example: The city was in a **welter **of confusion and chaos following the unexpected earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Turmoil **means a state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.
 
 
• For example, "The country was in **turmoil **after the sudden death of its leader."
 
 
 
• **Laconic **means using very few words, terse, or concise.
 
 
• For example, "His **laconic **reply to the question left us all puzzled and confused."
 
 
 
• **Difficult **means needing much effort or skill to accomplish, challenging or hard to deal with.
 
 
• For example, "The exam was **difficult**, requiring students to apply their knowledge in new and creative ways."
 
 
 
• **Vile **means extremely unpleasant, morally bad, or wicked.
 
 
• For example, "The **vile **odor emanating from the garbage dump made it difficult to breathe."
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

Reticence

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

The boss has instructed all of us to finish the project by tomorrow, (isn't it)?
questions.solution:
Since the sentence ends with a question mark, there should be a question tag at the end of the assertive sentence. You put a negative question tag at the end of a positive sentence and a positive question tag at the end of a negative sentence. Therefore, option 3 can be eliminated.

Also, the tense of the tag is determined by the tense of the auxiliary/modal verb of the statement that precedes it. Since in the given sentence ‘has’ is the auxiliary verb, ‘hasn’t she’ would be the correct question tag.

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

Garima has her meal at three, (when she has it), she goes off to sleep.

options.text: when she will have had it

questions.solution: The given sentence means that after Garima eats her meal at three, she goes off to sleep. The present perfect tense **(sub + has/have + v3 + object)** should be used here to make the sentence grammatically correct. To *have* something means to eat and *had* indicates the past participle form. Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is not the key concern of the businesses these days?

questions.question: Which of the following reason is not being mentioned in the passage in regard to people leaving their jobs?

dissatisfaction with opportunities at current job
better compensation and benefits in new job

questions.solution: According to the given passage, *30 percent leave* (their jobs)* for **better compensation and benefits**, 27 percent for a better career opportunity, 27 percent for **new experience**, 21 percent are **dissatisfied with opportunities at current job**, and 16 percent desire to change careers or industries*. Only option 1 has not been mentioned here which makes it the correct answer.

questions.question: What does feel good factor mean with respect to employees?

options.text: opportunity given to employees to work abroad
anything which can keep employees happy and satisfied

questions.solution: The passage talks about giving employees incentives (other than monetary) in order to retain them in the respective business. So the feel good factor refers to *anything which can keep employees happy and satisfied.* Options 2 and 3 are not mentioned in the passage and can be eliminated.

questions.question: What can be the suitable title for the passage?

options.text: Money – a major motivator for employees
Giving employees a feel good factor

questions.solution:
The passage discusses how employees can be retained by employers by providing useful incentives. This means than other than money they should be given a feel good factor so that they do not switch their jobs. Thus, option 3 is the most apt title for the passage.

The passage does not talk about any incentive, but those which would motivate the employees. Thus, option 1 can be eliminated. Rather than posing the difficulty in retaining the employees as a challenge, the passage discusses about the feel good factors which should be provided keeping in mind the various reasons why people switch jobs. This eliminates option 4 as a potential answer.
